changes.description: Park and continue. Put the open ticket on hold with a staff-entered label or the first product as a fallback, then open a fresh sale.
Per-register parking storage. Parked tickets survive a page reload or browser restart on the same browser profile and stay scoped to the selected register.
Visible parked count. The ticket toolbar exposes the current count and responds to parking changes made from another tab in the same browser.
Version-pinned recall. Reopening a hold verifies the original server session, terminal and menu version, then restores its lines, fulfillment and adjustments.
Active-ticket protection. Recall remains disabled while another ticket has items. Staff can park or finish the current ticket before recalling a hold.
Confirmed discard. Staff can remove a named hold through an explicit confirmation without changing the open ticket.
Register sales history. Recent sales show the number, amount, timestamp, tender, menu version and refund status for this register.
Historical receipt and reprint. Open and print a recent receipt while keeping the current register ticket in place.
Staff note. Add a 240-character internal note with a live character count and preserve it through refresh, parking and sale submission.
Discount presets. Apply or remove a 10% staff discount or 15% service recovery discount against the server quote.
Tip quick amounts. Set no tip, $1, $2 or $5 in the adjustment dialog.
Custom tip. Enter a tip of up to $50 in whole cents with inline validation before applying it.
Itemized adjustment totals. Display authoritative discount, tax, tip and grand total in the ticket, adjusted payment review and printed receipt.,
Live sold-out controls. Store-specific inventory updates disable unavailable catalogue and quick keys without a reload.
Remaining quantities. Limited-stock keys show the units left after accounting for this ticket. Quantity controls prevent adding past that limit.
Recoverable stock rejection. If stock changes before payment, the register refreshes availability, keeps the ticket and returns staff to editing.
Editable quick keys. Assign four distinct products to terminal-specific shortcuts that persist in the browser.
Cashier keyboard guide. A visible shortcuts panel explains keyboard navigation, including F6 for parking, F7 for recall, F8 for recent sales and F9 for adjustments.
One-action search reset. The reset button or Escape clears the query and category together and returns focus to search.
Keyboard product navigation. Arrow keys move between category buttons and within the product grid, skipping unavailable items. Arrow Down from search focuses the first available product.
Fixed desktop payment area. The product grid and ticket lines scroll independently at workstation sizes so payment remains in view.
Larger touch targets. Category, service, parking, quantity and cash controls meet a 44px target height, with 44×44px quantity buttons.
Add cash bills. Add $1, $5, $10 or $20 to the received amount and calculate change as bills are counted.
Last-used tender. Start the next sale with the last successfully recorded payment method for that register in the same tab.
Live customer counter. Open the display for this register and broadcast ticket, payment, completion and idle states with no staff notes or transaction IDs.,,
Terminals can fetch the canonical tender limits, note limit, tax rate, and discount menu through the POS policy endpoint.
A cashier can apply approved 10% staff or 15% service-recovery discounts. The server computes the amount from the selected preset.
A discount reduces the taxable subtotal. The receipt exposes the adjusted base and rounds the resulting tax in whole cents.
Cashiers can add a tip after tax. The server validates the entered cents and caps tips at $50.
Cashiers can attach a staff note. The API cleans line endings, trims whitespace, and checks length and control characters.
Cash tender enforces an upper limit in addition to checking that the amount covers the sale. Cash change reflects the final discounted and tipped total.
The saved receipt retains the applied adjustment amounts, note, tender, store, and signed menu version for later reads.
Sale retries include normalized adjustments in their request identity. Earlier unadjusted receipts can still be read and retried with their original idempotency keys.
A terminal can load its own recent receipts from the ledger, with a bounded result limit.
Registers and operations can query availability overrides for a specific store. Other storefronts keep their own stock.
Staff can mark an item out of stock even when it normally has unlimited availability.
Staff can set a finite count or reset an item to unlimited availability.
Consuming the last counted unit makes the item unavailable automatically.
Quotes flag unavailable items before tender and identify the SKU, store, and remaining count.
Stock validation counts the same SKU across differently customized lines.
Checkout commits stock consumption and the receipt in one transaction. Retrying a successful sale leaves stock untouched.
Connected views receive an inventory event when staff changes an override or a sale consumes counted stock.
The audit trail identifies manual stock changes and stock exhaustion by store and item.
Operations can record a full demo refund against the original charged amount. The original tender and receipt remain available alongside the refund record.
The refund ledger enforces one refund per sale and a unique operation key. An exact retry returns the original refund.
Refunds require a bounded staff reason and record an audit event with the order number, store, and amount.
Refunded orders move out of active kitchen and pickup work, show separately in order counts, and cannot advance in the kitchen.
Sales reports filter by storefront and inclusive UTC dates. A later refund counts in the period when it was posted.
Sales reports reconcile gross item sales, discounts, taxes, tips, charges, refunds, and net receipts by storefront, day, and overall.
The same filtered report can be downloaded as CSV for reconciliation. The export contains aggregate amounts and excludes staff notes and refund reasons.
The kitchen workboard separates New, Preparing, and Ready tickets and shows the count in each lane.
A store selector limits the board to one location and saves that selection in the URL.
Drinks, Patisserie, and Kitchen station filters route tickets using the item’s menu category and highlight the matching quantities.
Mixed-station tickets retain their other items and identify when a station’s bump action affects the whole ticket.
Each ticket shows a live elapsed clock. Ready tickets show time since they were marked Ready.
Waiting tickets at eight minutes or more receive an overdue label and contribute to the overdue count.
Overdue only narrows the screen to delayed work and preserves the choice in the URL.
Kitchen cards expose line quantities, selected modifiers, service type, store, and the total number of items.
Cashier ticket notes appear separately above the prep lines.
A large action on each card starts prep, marks the order Ready, or records handoff. A pending action cannot submit again.
Left and right arrows select a ticket and B bumps it. The selected ticket has a visible outline and keyboard focus follows it when possible.
Long item and modifier lists scroll inside the card, with the bump control outside that scroll area. Larger wall displays fit two cards per lane.
The board receives live order changes, polls as a fallback, and disables bump controls while its order feed is offline.
Availability opens a separate stock view for each store and displays its current state.
Stock can be searched by product or category and narrowed to unavailable items or limited quantities.
Staff can mark a product unavailable and restore it. The view distinguishes staff blocks from exhausted stock.
Staff can set a finite stock quantity, see the remaining count, or clear the quantity for unlimited stock.
A full demo refund requires confirmation and a reason. Uncertain responses can be retried using the original request key.
Refunded sales have a dedicated order filter and display the amount, reason, and recorded time. They cannot be advanced from the queue.
Sales totals can be filtered by store and inclusive UTC dates, with charges, discounts, taxes, tips, refunds, and net collections displayed.
The sales screen breaks the filtered figures down by store and calendar day.
The download button exports CSV with the same filters as the displayed report.
The public pickup display can enter and exit full screen from its toolbar.
On supported devices, the pickup attendant can keep the screen awake. The display reacquires the lock when visible again and reports when the lock is unavailable.
Pickup numbers newly moved to Ready receive a one-minute highlight and a screen-reader announcement.

name: Counter display, terminal lab and sales

changes.description: Dedicated customer display separates the customer view from staff controls.
Register chooser pairs the counter display with a specific simulated terminal.
Register pairing persists in a shareable device URL and falls back to a valid terminal.
The display requests a current ticket on opening, so a screen can join a sale in progress.
Welcome, active ticket, payment and receipt states give the customer phase-specific instructions.
The buyer can verify line quantities, modifier names, line prices and service type while the cashier edits.
A transaction breakdown separates discounts, tax, tips and the total and marks a pending quote.
At checkout, the customer display shows the pickup number and the versioned pickup instructions.
The display clears stale ticket content if the register stops responding, then tries to reconnect.
The display projects only bounded customer-visible values and uses text rendering for live fields.
Optional fullscreen keeps the facing screen usable as a dedicated counter appliance.
High-contrast responsive counter typography and de-duplicated live announcements support at-a-glance and assistive reading.
Terminal Lab offers documented seller, customer, compact and scaled browser profiles.
Custom dimensions and rotation test layouts beyond the built-in profiles.
The same preview can load the register, customer screen, kitchen board, kiosk, pickup, operations or sales surface.
Fit-to-window preview retains the embedded page's actual CSS layout dimensions.
Diagnostics measure horizontal overflow using the embedded document.
The preview measures primary register touch targets against 44 CSS pixels and identifies undersized controls.
Diagnostics export a JSON snapshot suitable for comparing builds and viewport regressions.
Sales report filters by store and supports today, recent periods and a custom UTC range.
Opened report date ranges and store filters can be shared as URLs.
The report breaks down gross, discounts, tax, tips, money collected, refunds and net collections.
A daily trend chart and detailed daily table expose the timing of sales and later refunds.
The store reconciliation table compares collected, refunded and net amounts across locations.
The selected report can be downloaded as CSV or printed with the input controls removed.
